What are a workspace, repository and wor: What are a workspace, repository and worktree?
A workspace groups projects for quick sw: A workspace groups projects for quick switching; it is not a Git submodule. A repository stores Git history. A worktree is a checkout with its own files, HEAD and staging area; linked worktrees share repository history. Switch repositories from the workspace picker; search and pagination help with long lists.
Each node is a commit; lines connect it: Each node is a commit; lines connect it to its parents. Branch and tag labels point to commits. HEAD marks your current checkout. A merge commit has multiple parents; a fast-forward moves a branch label without adding a merge node. Select a row to inspect its files and diff. Right-click a commit for available actions.
How do I switch branches or open a remot: How do I switch branches or open a remote branch?
Use the branch picker, or double-click a: Use the branch picker, or double-click a graph node or branch label to enter checkout review. Inspect the destination before confirming. Opening a remote branch can create a local tracking branch. Switching the parent repository does not silently update submodule checkouts.
How are Stage, Unstage and Discard diffe: How are Stage, Unstage and Discard different?
Stage copies the selected changes into t: Stage copies the selected changes into the next commit’s staging area. Unstage removes them from that area while keeping working files. Discard restores the reviewed scope and can remove new files. Review its exact scope before confirming; recovery information is shown after supported operations.
Can I stage just part of a file?: Can I stage just part of a file?
What do Fetch, Pull, Push and Refresh do: What do Fetch, Pull, Push and Refresh do?
Fetch downloads remote history without m: Fetch downloads remote history without merging into your local branch. Pull fetches and integrates into the current branch using the reviewed method. Push publishes selected local history. Refresh rereads local Git state; it does not replace Fetch. Network actions use configured credentials or SSH.
What do the up and down counts mean?: What do the up and down counts mean?
↑ counts local commits missing from the: ↑ counts local commits missing from the tracked remote branch; ↓ counts remote commits missing locally. Both can be nonzero when histories diverge. These counts describe the last fetched remote state, not live server state. Fetch before deciding how to integrate.
How do Stash, Apply and Pop work?: How do Stash, Apply and Pop work?
Stash saves unfinished work. Apply resto: Stash saves unfinished work. Apply restores it onto the currently checked-out branch and keeps the stash. Pop restores it there and removes the stash only after success. You can stash on main, switch to develop, then pop onto develop. Conflicts keep the stash. Finish an active Git operation before restoring another stash.
How do Merge and Fast-forward differ?: How do Merge and Fast-forward differ?
Merge combines histories into the curren: Merge combines histories into the current branch. Create merge commit retains both tips as parents, making the junction visible. Fast-forward is available when the current tip is an ancestor of the incoming tip; it only advances the branch. Optional source deletion removes only the eligible local source branch after a verified successful merge.
What is Cherry-pick? Why choose a parent: What is Cherry-pick? Why choose a parent?
Cherry-pick applies one commit’s changes: Cherry-pick applies one commit’s changes onto your current branch as a new commit. A merge commit has multiple parents, so choose the baseline used to calculate those changes. Parent 1 is usually the destination branch before the merge; compare the preview before selecting it. Parent 2 produces a different delta.
Amend replaces the last commit using the: Amend replaces the last commit using the reviewed message and staged content; its ID changes. It does not combine arbitrary older commits. Revert creates a new commit undoing a selected commit’s changes. Prefer a new revert when preserving shared history matters.
How do I resolve a conflict?: How do I resolve a conflict?
Open Working changes and select a confli: Open Working changes and select a conflict. Compare Current and Incoming, choose individual text blocks or edit Result, then review and stage the resolved result. Continue or commit the pending operation only after every conflict is resolved. Current/Incoming refer to the shown operation, especially during rebase. Binary and submodule conflicts need their dedicated choices.
A submodule is a separate Git repository: A submodule is a separate Git repository referenced by a recorded commit in its parent. Each parent branch can record a different commit. Recorded, staged and checked-out commits can differ. Dirty means files inside changed; Commit changed means the checkout differs from the recorded pointer. Detached HEAD is normal when checking out a recorded submodule commit.

How do I clone or publish a new reposito: How do I clone or publish a new repository?
Clone from the workspace picker into a n: Clone from the workspace picker into a new folder. To publish local work, commit first and use Push. If no remote exists, Add remote lets you use an existing repository URL or create an empty GitHub/GitLab repository using a global Connection. Repository creation, local remote setup and Push are separate reviewed steps. Choose visibility carefully.
How do I create and push a version tag?: How do I create and push a version tag?
Right-click the desired commit and choos: Right-click the desired commit and choose Create tag. Review the name and exact commit. A local tag is not published by a normal branch push; use the tag’s Push action and review the destination. Existing remote tags are not silently overwritten.
How do I open a pull request or merge re: How do I open a pull request or merge request?
Use the branch’s request action and veri: Use the branch’s request action and verify the source → target direction. Publish the source branch first. GitHub calls it a pull request; GitLab calls it a merge request. The host connection needs the relevant API permissions. Creating a request does not itself merge the branches.
What does Copy commit link copy?: What does Copy commit link copy?
It copies the selected commit’s full rem: It copies the selected commit’s full remote web URL. GitNova uses the current branch’s fetch upstream, then origin, then a sole configured remote. Global Connections identify private Git hosts. No token is needed just to form a link. A local-only commit may not open for teammates until pushed; a link does not grant access.
Where do I configure accounts and CI?: Where do I configure accounts and CI?
Open Settings → Connections. Host accoun: Open Settings → Connections. Host accounts apply globally to matching Git hosts, not one repository. CI status appears between Commit message and Author when configured and available. GitLab pipelines and configured Jenkins evidence are read from their services, not from local Git alone. Git transport credentials/SSH are separate from provider API tokens; tokens stay in Keychain.

Use a linked worktree to keep another ch: Use a linked worktree to keep another checkout of the same repository, for example to review a release while keeping feature work open.
